audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Graves / Skill / Yone / Yone / Graves / Yone / Yone; the packet and the audited mirror both read Graves / Graves / Skill / Yone / Yone / Yone / Yone. The difficulty label also said TRICKY 7.5/10 on a 50.54% win rate over 8568 games, and the mirror already reset its own side to EVEN.
audit.why: Level 2 is still his — End of the Line plus shotgun autos beat an unstacked Mortal Steel — and level 3 is where your Q chain evens it, which is exactly what whys[1] and whys[2] already said. Nothing about level 6 favours him: Collateral Damage is a 100s single-target shell, while Fate Sealed catches him once Quickdraw is spent.
audit.corrected: Graves, Graves, Skill, Yone, Yone, Yone, Yone; difficulty EVEN at 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Graves power spike and no cooldowns appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 down to 12s and its cooldown drops every time he lands an auto; Smoke Screen is 26s at rank 1, the longest gap in his kit; End of the Line 13s to 6s; Collateral Damage 100/80/60s. Your Soul Unbound falls 22s to 10s and Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: His real spikes are Quickdraw rank-ups and items; yours are level 3, Soul Unbound's shrinking cooldown, and the first crit item. The Smoke Screen window at 26s is the longest punish window in the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names throughout the content layer — 'Buckshot' for his Q and 'Dash' for his E — plus Fate Sealed described as setting up team knockups.
audit.why: Graves's Q is End of the Line and his E is Quickdraw. End of the Line detonates after 1 second OR on contact with terrain, so fighting near a wall makes it land instantly instead of after the travel delay. Quickdraw grants armour and MR, doubled if he dashes toward you, and refreshes off his autos — so it is a resistance buff as much as an escape. Smoke Screen reduces sight range rather than blinding. Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls; the knockup in this matchup is your own Mortal Steel at two stacks.
audit.corrected: Names corrected to End of the Line and Quickdraw; stay off walls so his shell keeps its full delay; treat Quickdraw as resistances plus mobility, and punish inside Smoke Screen's 26-second cooldown.

edits.after: Graves owns the first two levels: his End of the Line (Q) plus shotgun autos deal more than your unstacked Mortal Steel can answer, so give ground and farm rather than contest early trades. Walking into his Smoke Screen (W), 26s at rank 1, just feeds him a free chunk.

edits.after: Level 3 evens out as your Q chain and Soul Unbound come online, and from level 4 the lane tilts to you — bait Quickdraw (E), 16s at rank 1, and punish the cooldown with a full all-in. His lane sustain is thin, so every trade you win sticks.

notes: Two fabricated ability names ran through the whole content layer: 'Buckshot' for End of the Line and 'Dash' for Quickdraw — both corrected everywhere they appeared. Chart flipped in matched pairs onto the packet, which the mirror also adopted, and the difficulty label moved from TRICKY 7.5/10 to EVEN 6/10 to match a 50.54% win rate over 8568 games. New mechanical content added: End of the Line detonates on terrain contact rather than only after its 1-second fuse, Quickdraw is a resistance buff whose cooldown shortens off autos, and Smoke Screen's 26s is the longest punish window in the lane.
